answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly signaling friction in the self-serve path where simplification has shown durable uplift before. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding drive activation and time-to-value. Verifying these will confirm whether the prior cohort effects hold and whether there are seasonal or cohort-specific caveats. Promotional pricing (memory_73) showed poor durability and retention harm; the competitor's aggressive cuts make it a race-to-bottom trap. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but don't address our current activation decline. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary lever we can layer after fixing onboarding friction. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment and slower sales cycle—not the immediate QoQ activation drop we're seeing in the main funnel. A simplified onboarding experiment targets the root friction signal, builds on proven SMB mechanics, and preserves sustainable unit economics against competitive pricing pressure.
